composition.note: 433000 dates composition to the years after the plague of 1348 and distinguishes early-1350s readers from the later Hamilton 90 autograph. The coarse interval reflects that existing dating language, not a claim of a precisely known decade-long composition.
composition.label: After 1348; circulating in the early 1350s

setting.note: The Florence plague of 1348 is the narrative frame; it is not the date of composition of every embedded tale.

witness.note: 433000 dates Boccaccio’s surviving Hamilton 90 autograph approximately to 1370; this is a late authorial witness, not first composition.
witness.label: c. 1370 · Hamilton 90

description: Examines storytelling within the plague frame, connecting selected or installment-specific tales to desire, wit, religion, household power, and social judgment. Covers Fortune, Ingenuity, and the Limits of Control; The Limits of Laughter: Violence, Deception, and Consent; Magnificence, Power, and the Problem of Griselda; From Shakespeare to Modern Readers: The Book’s Afterlife.
